No commit hash, no per-document SHA-256 pin, and no verbatim dated approval quotation exists anywhere in this feature's allowed inputs specifically naming a 'ruling C(1)' or 'ruling C(2)'. Per the calibration's own evidence bar (spec-review-calibration.md, 'Amendment Re-Review Context'), a declaration this incomplete does not suppress the default Phase-1 judgment, and the default judgment treats a Pending-status package's own citation of quality-gate/adversarial-review ('cross-model panel') material, with no citable, verifiable approval record backing it, as an unauthorized/unverifiable approval-boundary gap -- a downstream reviewer, task author, or verifier has no way to confirm the two new Block conditions' own stated rationale rests on a real, dated human ruling rather than an unverified or fabricated assertion, which is exactly the property this gate's evidence bar exists to guarantee. This contrasts with every other adversarial-review citation in the same document (B1-B9, M1-M10), each of which is backed by a fully-evidenced INV-020/INV-021 entry in investigation.md -- the C(1)/C(2) citations are the sole exception to that established, otherwise-consistent evidentiary practice.
